FLY TYING / BEGINNERS

How to tie a Pheasant Tail Nymph

One fly, eight clear steps. Gather the materials, follow each stage, and check the finished shape before you start the next one.

By Castward Updated 11 November 2026
At a glance
Pattern
Pheasant Tail Nymph
Lesson
8 illustrated steps
Goal
Secure wraps • clear eye
Start here

Quick answer

Take one stage at a time. Keep the hook eye clear, use only the material the step needs, and check each tie-in before you move on.

On this page

  1. Lay out the materials
  2. Tie it, one step at a time
  3. Your finished fly
  4. Small mistakes, simple fixes
  5. Common questions

01

Lay out the materials

These sizes are a starting recipe. Test the hook and materials together before you tie a batch.[1]

Swipe the table to compare all columns.

PartFor this version
HookSize 14, 2X-long nymph hook
ThreadBrown 6/0
Tail, body, wingcasePheasant tail fibers
RibSmall copper wire
ThoraxPeacock herl
02

Tie it, one step at a time

  1. 01

    Lay the foundation

    Cover the shank with brown thread. Bind copper wire along its side, with the free end at the bend.

    Bench tip Leave a little space behind the eye.

  2. 02

    Measure the tail

    Tie in aligned pheasant fibers. Aim for a tail about three-quarters of the shank length.

    Bench tip Keep the fiber tips together.

  3. 03

    Wrap the abdomen

    Wind the fiber butts forward to cover the rear two-thirds. Tie off and trim.

    Bench tip Keep space for the thorax.

  4. 04

    Add the copper rib

    Spiral the wire forward opposite the body wraps. Tie off, then break away the excess.

    Bench tip Do not use fine scissors on wire.

  5. 05

    Set the wingcase

    Tie a new pheasant bundle at the thorax rear, with its long butts pointing back.

    Bench tip Save the forward tips for the legs.

  6. 06

    Build the thorax

    Tie in peacock herl. Wind a small thorax, then secure and trim.

    Bench tip Keep the thorax slightly fuller than the abdomen.

  7. 07

    Close the wingcase

    Pull the butts over the thorax. Secure behind the eye and trim; sweep the saved tips down each side.

    Bench tip Do not cover the eye with fibers.

  8. 08

    Finish the fly

    Whip finish behind the eye. Cut the thread and check the wingcase stays put.

    Bench tip A gentle tug finds loose materials.

[1]
03

Your finished fly

  • ✓The hook eye stays clear.
  • ✓The materials stay put under a gentle tug.
  • ✓The point and hook gap remain usable.
04

Small mistakes, simple fixes

Swipe the table to compare all columns.

What you seeTry this
A thick abdomenUse fewer fibers and less thread.
Loose bodyUse the copper rib to secure the fibers.
Crowded thoraxReserve the front third before you start the body.
A few good questions

Before you head out

Can I change the color?

Yes. Keep the same sequence and use comparable materials. Change one feature at a time so you can see its effect.

What if the fly looks uneven?

Check the secure wraps and open eye first. Keep this fly as a reference, then repeat the recipe with less material.
